summary:
All 5 fixtures hand-trace cleanly against the actual JS parser at index.html:2870-2900 (parseInsightMarker uses lastIndexOf on the literal '

---DEEP-DIVES---
', then per-line split with ' :: ' and a 3-element pad). Each fixture's HTML header comment matches what the parser would produce. Fixture quality is high: realistic markdown, every fixture has a documentation-comment that names the case + expected output, exercises the documented edge case. The 8 deferred TDD anchors in section 'TDD Anchor' name behavioral assertions (extract three topics, last marker wins, javascript: stripped, 100 deltas coalesce to 1 render) — these are good behavioral tests, not substring-presence checks. NO critical fixture is missing for cases the parser MUST handle. Significant uncovered paths (CRLF line endings, partial marker across delta boundary, mid-stream debounce coalescing under load, Mermaid render error fallback path, link sanitizer scheme rejection) are documented below and should be picked up by the deferred test follow-up — not blockers for this task per Decision 9 (tests deferred, fixtures + hand-trace are the gate).

uncovered_paths.issue:
INSIGHT_MARKER literal is '

---DEEP-DIVES---
'. If Swift forwards a buffer that uses CRLF (e.g. an LLM that emits Windows-style newlines, or pasted content), the buffer between paragraphs is '

---DEEP-DIVES---
', which does NOT contain the LF-only '

' sequence. lastIndexOf returns -1 and the marker is missed entirely — body would render the topic list as markdown bullets and the deep-dive pane would stay empty. No fixture exercises this. Per-line CR strip ('line.replace(/$/, '')') only handles per-line CR after split — it does NOT normalize the boundary.
uncovered_paths.fix_recommendation: Either (a) add buffer-level normalization at the top of parseInsightMarker: 'buffer = buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, \'\n\');' before the lastIndexOf call, or (b) commit a 'crlf.md' fixture (saved with CRLF line endings, document expected behavior) and either fix the parser or document the LF-only contract explicitly in the marker spec. Recommend (a) — defensive normalization is one line and handles the realistic LLM/pasted-content case.

uncovered_paths.path: Partial marker arriving across two appendInsightDelta calls
uncovered_paths.issue:
The Details section explicitly calls out: 'Stream interrupted mid-marker (

---DEEP-DI with no closing): no match, render full buffer as markdown until next chunk arrives.' Current parser handles this correctly (lastIndexOf returns -1 on partial substring), but no fixture documents it. A future test should append delta1 = 'body...

---DEEP-DI', verify topics = [] and body preserved, then append delta2 = 'VES---
- Topic :: hint :: file.md', verify topics = 1 after the second render.
uncovered_paths.fix_recommendation: Add 'partial-marker.md' fixture OR add a TDD anchor 'test_partial_marker_across_chunks_resolves_on_completion' in the InsightMarkerParserTests / InsightDebounceTests follow-up. Not strictly required to add a fixture — partial-marker behavior is testable by the existing happy.md content split at an arbitrary byte index.

uncovered_paths.issue: TDD anchor 'test_rapid_deltas_coalesce' covers '100 deltas in 50 ms → exactly 1 render after ~150 ms'. Good behavioral assertion. But there is no anchor for the case where deltas arrive over a longer window (e.g. 5 deltas, each 200 ms apart, 1 second total) — the expected behavior is 5 renders (each clearTimeout/setTimeout cycle elapses). Without that, the debounce semantics are under-specified: a buggy implementation that uses setInterval, or a too-large debounce, would still pass the rapid-coalesce test.
uncovered_paths.fix_recommendation: Add a second anchor 'test_spaced_deltas_render_separately' — N deltas spaced > 150 ms apart → N renders. Pairs with test_rapid_deltas_coalesce to fully constrain the debounce contract.

uncovered_paths.issue: processInsightMermaidBlocks at index.html:2906-2944 has a per-block try/catch that on failure restores raw <pre><code> + an .insight-mermaid-error label. This is critical Decision 7 / Decision 10 behavior (a single bad diagram must not abort the rest of the render) but is not in the TDD anchor list. No fixture and no anchor.
uncovered_paths.fix_recommendation: Add a fixture 'mermaid-mixed.md' (one valid mermaid block + one syntactically broken mermaid block + trailing markdown) and an anchor 'test_one_bad_mermaid_does_not_abort_render' — assert the valid block renders, the bad block shows raw fence + error label, the trailing markdown renders.

uncovered_paths.issue: TDD anchor 'test_javascript_href_stripped' covers javascript: scheme. Good. But the implementation rejects javascript:/data:/file:/vbscript: AND any unknown scheme, while allowing http(s):// and relative paths. The other rejected schemes (data:, file:, vbscript:, mailto: which would be unknown) and the relative-path allow case are not in the anchor list.
uncovered_paths.fix_recommendation: Expand the InsightSanitizationTests anchor list to enumerate each rejected scheme (data:, file:, vbscript:) and explicitly assert that http://, https://, and relative paths like '../foo.md' or '/path/to.md' are preserved. Each scheme should be one anchor — substring presence is not enough; the assertion must be on the rendered <a> tag's href attribute (or its absence).

uncovered_paths.issue: appendInsightDelta at index.html:3138 rejects deltas whose sessionId does not match state.insightSessionId. This is correct race-condition handling for session switches mid-stream. No anchor documents this behavior.
uncovered_paths.fix_recommendation: Add anchor 'test_stale_session_delta_dropped' — call loadInsightView({sessionId:'A'}), then appendInsightDelta('B', 'should-not-appear'); assert insightBufferText is unchanged.

fixture_quality.notes: Every fixture starts with an HTML comment block naming the fixture, its purpose, and the expected parser output (body description + topics array with explicit labels/hints/scopeHints). This is exactly the right format for hand-trace review and as golden inputs for the deferred Swift XCTests. Fixtures are small (17-30 lines), realistic markdown content, no formatting issues, no trailing whitespace problems observed. The in-code-fence.md fixture is particularly well-crafted: it places the 'fake' marker inside a syntactically valid markdown code fence so a real markdown parser would also keep it inert, and it uses lastIndexOf semantics rather than relying on the parser to detect 'inside-fence' context.

tdd_anchor_quality.notes: All 8 anchors describe behavioral assertions (extract N topics, last marker wins, scheme stripped, 100 deltas → 1 render). None are substring-presence checks. Naming follows test_<scenario>_<expected> convention. Anchors map 1:1 to fixtures plus 2 sanitization + 1 debounce. Recommend adding the 4 anchors called out in uncovered_paths (CRLF normalization, spaced-delta debounce, mermaid per-block fallback, expanded scheme matrix, stale-session) when the deferred test infrastructure lands — not blockers for this task.
